statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-63075 ("QUIC ACK-only Packet Retention Can Cause Memory Exhaustion", Low): the QUIC stack keeps metadata for every ACK-only packet it sends, so a peer that completes a handshake, keeps eliciting ACKs and never acknowledges them can grow connection memory until denial of service. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.8; the FIPS modules are not affected because the QUIC code is outside the FIPS module boundary. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260825.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/7c98d79738549df92868e7dd9be4bbf061eed709, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.8. Alpine fixed it in openssl 3.5.8-r0 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-63075). The published DHI Alpine 3.23 builds from the openssl source (the main repository packages, and the openssl-fips FIPS-provider package in the DHI enterprise repository, built from the same source at matching versions from 3.5.5_git20260330-r1 on) are 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2, each on x86_64 and aarch64. The libcrypto in every one of these builds reports the OpenSSL release of its package version (3.5.5_git20260330-r1, a git snapshot dated 30 March 2026, reports 3.5.5). Builds before 3.5.8-r0 are based on OpenSSL 3.5.7 or earlier, and 3.5.8-r0 and every later build on OpenSSL 3.5.8 or later. The libssl exports the QUIC methods (OSSL_QUIC_client_method(), OSSL_QUIC_server_method()) in each build checked (3.5.4-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1 and 3.5.9-r2, both architectures). The openssl-fips package holds only the FIPS provider (fips.so, built from the same OpenSSL release as the package version in every build on both architectures) and its configuration files; the advisory places the affected code outside the FIPS module boundary.

CVE-2026-63075 ("QUIC ACK-only Packet Retention Can Cause Memory Exhaustion", Low): the QUIC stack keeps metadata for every ACK-only packet it sends, so a peer that completes a handshake, keeps eliciting ACKs and never acknowledges them can grow connection memory until denial of service. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.8; the FIPS modules are not affected because the QUIC code is outside the FIPS module boundary. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260825.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/7c98d79738549df92868e7dd9be4bbf061eed709, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.8. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u2 (DSA-6465-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-63075). The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds, and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build, only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64: 25 versions, 17 standard and 8 FIPS builds, based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. No build based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1 or 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-63075. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, the fixed boundary here, and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u2 entry naming it. The fix adds the function ossl_ackm_on_tx_ack_only_packet(): the libssl debug symbols list it in the first standard and FIPS rebuilds of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, and not in the last standard and FIPS rebuilds of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, on both architectures (upstream OpenSSL 3.5.7 does not contain it, so it comes from Debian's backport). The libssl in every one of these builds, on both architectures, exports the QUIC methods (OSSL_QUIC_client_method(), OSSL_QUIC_server_method()). Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the build's own OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory places the affected code outside the FIPS module boundary, and the FIPS builds' libcrypto and libssl are Debian's 3.5 libraries checked above.
